chunks: Ali ibn Ibrahim, from his father, from Abdullah ibn al-Mughira, from Abdullah ibn Sinan, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), who said:

The Messenger of Allah (peace be upon him and his family) prayed Asr with the people, so he shortened the two final cycles. When he finished, the people said to him, 'Did something happen during the prayer?' He said, 'And what is that?' They said, 'You shortened the two final cycles.' So he said to them, 'Did you not hear the child crying?'
ai.seo_question: Why did the Prophet shorten the last two rak'ahs of Dhuhr prayer?
ai.summary: Recorded in al-Kafi, this hadith illustrates the Prophet’s (peace be upon him and his family) practical application of mercy (rahma) by shortening the Dhuhr prayer upon hearing a child's cry, a practice later codified in Shia jurisprudence as a recommended act (mustahabb) to alleviate the child's distress. It underscores the principle that religious rituals should accommodate human needs, particularly the vulnerability of children, reflecting the broader Islamic ethic of compassion in communal worship.
